summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2016 under Jenny Purtle, having also studied under teachers including Susan L. and John C. Huntington.

Sarah E. Fraser works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, she became an associate professor at Northwestern University in 1996 and directrice d'études at the EPHE in 2000.

Sarah Harding (b. 1951) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpon Lama Tenpa. She served on the faculty at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and became a Tsadra Foundation fellow around 2001.

Sarah Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indologist. She completed an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an M.A. post there as of 2026.

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She held affiliations with Oxford's Oriental Studies Faculty, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (b. 1914) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. A student of Jitendra Nath Banerjea, he served as librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943 and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Presidency University and University of Calcutta, he was director of the Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Manipur University under S. Shyamkishor Singh, also studying under S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He pursued a Sinhala-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Deshapriya Gunasena / G. A. Gamini (attested 2026).

Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1988–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1999–2005).
Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at the University of Madras, Presidency College, Madras Christian College, and Balliol College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975), a philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College, held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities, President of Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Chancellor of Delhi University.
Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and served on the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen was an Indologist and sinologist who studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satis Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Sarat Chandra Das and at Calcutta University (PhD), later serving as Principal of Sanskrit College and Professor of Sanskrit and Pali at Presidency University.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1951) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 1999, 2026).
